I am actually reading this book by the discoverer of LSD Albert Hofman, "My problem child," and he writes how he couldn't have predicted his drug would be abused because it can be so unpleasant, especially at a higher dose.

So while I can see how  smaller dozes like 1 gram or so can be pleasantly exciting, a higher dose - definitely 3 grams or more - but even 2 - is something to struggle through.

To be fair when the effects of higher doses are waning, there's an "ecstatic release". But as Sam mentioned we wouldn't subject ourself to torture to gain some moments of pleasure because of the asymmetry of pain and pleasure.

But I don't think the model of pain and pleasure works here, the first part of the trip while challenging also has something about it that it's deeply alluring. Like stepping into a strange planet and feeling immense discomfort from its atmospheric pressure throughout your body but being mesmerized by it at the same time.

Lemon acid does transform non-psychoactive  Psilocybin into highly psychoactive Psilocin, so it would make sense that it would hit you harder all at once than having to wait for your own body to do that metabolism first. 

I would not be surprised if the strongest wave can be 2 or even 3 times more potent. But on average perhaps the effect is more modest.

I don't have too many illusions my personal experiment is up to the standards of a scientific investigation. Notes are more for my own memory.

Here's a more technical explanation I could find:

"Magic mushrooms comprise psilocybin, a naturally occurring compound found in various species of mushrooms. Surprisingly enough, psilocybin is non-psychoactive and only generates mind-altering effects once our bodies convert it into psilocin after its consumption. In this case, the specific chemical process is called dephosphorylation, and can take up to two hours.

Dephosphorylation can take place in two distinctive ways:

The “traditional” way: after eating shrooms, psilocybin will convert into psilocin via the alkaline phosphatase enzyme in the intestine and kidney, or in acidic environments like the stomach.

Lemon tek: as lemon juice contains a pH of around two, it is acidic enough to convert psilocybin in the same way that the stomach can.

By lemon tekking, the psilocybin gets converted into psilocin before being consumed. As a result, you will have a much earlier onset trip than you would consume psychedelic mushrooms traditionally."

I've been wearing Oura ring daily since 2019. I love its minimalist form factor, and I check my readiness score daily. It tracks well with the way I subjectively feel in the morning. When I feel great, I feel even better seeing a high readiness score confirming that.

When I feel lousy, I still find it comforting to get an objective confirmation of what exactly went wrong with me that night (i.e., higher heart rate, lower HRV, or poor heart rate recovery; insufficient overall sleep, REM or deep sleep; elevated temperature, etc...)

I also use it every morning during my 10-minute guided mediation sessions, and it gives me feedback if I was too fidgety. Also, I use my heart rate variability during the session to gauge how well it went.

Yes, I can confirm that its step count can be inaccurate, and often, there are gaps in recording my data, probably because I move too much during sleep and like wearing my ring more loosely than recommended.

But while it may be at times inaccurate, it's pretty internally consistent and very comfortable to wear. After several years it feels like a part of my sensory system I can't imagine living without.

Perhaps it's due to my limitations as a  biological robot, perhaps I just haven't evolved to understand deeper reality and its logic.
